name: Yudhveer
description: An Indian mythological action game that runs in your browser. Cel-shaded sword-and-shield combat with sparks, hit-stop and bosses that block and parry back, across five worlds from a moonlit stepwell to a snow summit under an eclipse. Three.js, Rapier, TypeScript, Vite.

paragraphs: An Indian mythological action game where the bosses block and parry back, built to run in a plain browser tab.

YUDHVEER (युद्धवीर, "warrior-hero") is a sword-and-shield action game drawn from Indian myth: moonlit stepwells, forest akhadas, sea cities and snow peaks, fought through with a lathi, a talwar, a mace and a khanda. You play a young yodha who starts with almost nothing and earns every weapon, every guard and every trick on the road, across a prologue and five chapters. Each chapter is its own world, with its own light, its own music and its own bosses.
features: A mace clash in Dwarka, in slow motion. Captured live from the game.

Combat with weight. Hit-stop on every blow, a flinch and a flash on whoever is struck, a camera that kicks with the hit, ribbon trails on the blades and chingaari: sparks thrown along the blade's path where steel meets…
Deflect or be hit. Meet a blow in the last 140 ms and the attacker is thrown off balance. Break its posture and it stays open: your blows land at 2.2 times the damage while it recovers.

Four weapons, earned on the road. The lathi, the talwar with its dhal, the blessed mace in two hands, and the magical khanda. Each has its own set of moves; a move he has not earned yet simply does not work.

Five worlds, and a prologue. A moonlit stepwell, a forest akhada that turns from sunset to night, lamp-lit caves, the rain-lashed sea city of Dwarka, and a snow summit under an eclipse. Every one has its own lighting,…
